finding.claim: Blind SSRF: the callbackUrl a subscriber supplies is stored with no validation. The server then POSTs the payload to it every minute. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist, and no block on internal, loopback, link-local or metadata addresses such as 169.254.169.254 or localhost. Any caller of /subscribe can make the server send requests to internal services. The response body is discarded, so the SSRF is blind. The payload is fixed by the server and is not caller-controlled.
finding.source: POST /subscribe body parameter callbackUrl (Jobs.subscribe, line 13). The route is assumed to be reachable by any caller; no auth code was found in the repo.
finding.sink: HttpClient.send(HttpRequest POST to URI.create(cb)) at Jobs.java:24

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-controlled URL
URL is stored in the static subscriptions map without any validation
notifyAll iterates over the stored callback URLs on the per-minute job
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI from the stored URL

finding.guards_checked: Searched the only file in the repo (src/Jobs.java). There is no validation in subscribe or notifyAll: no scheme, host or IP checks, and no DNS-rebinding defence. There is no auth or route layer in the repo to check, so the entry is assumed from the comment on line 12. The HttpClient does not follow redirects by default, which does not mitigate a direct request to an internal URL.

verdict.guard_found: none (the only validation in the file is the anchored regex in thumb() at Jobs.java:30, which covers /thumb and not the callback path)
verdict.reason: Jobs.java:13-14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated, and Jobs.java:19-24 reads it back through URI.create(cb) and client.send with no scheme or host check; the route is assumed to be unauthenticated because the repo has no auth code.
